public_rationale: The broad observation of continuing lawyer problems is supported, and an archived May 25, 2025 page verifies 112 total database cases. But that total includes self-represented litigants. I could not verify the 914 endpoint or establish comparable lawyer-only counts. These gaps prevent a supported judgment on the combined numerical claim. They also prevent a precise assessment of how much of the claimed growth applies to lawyers.
limitations: Database totals count recorded decisions, not necessarily distinct lawyers or incidents.
A missing accessible snapshot is not evidence that the claimed count was false.
Growth in recorded cases does not measure the rate of hallucinations among all lawyers using LLMs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As far as he knows, a lot of lawyers who use LLMs are having problems with hallucinations, and documented cases of lawyers called out in Damien Charlotin's database rose from 112 less than a year ago to 914, which he calls 8x growth in less than 12 months.

statement.excerpt: And as far as I know, a lot of lawyers who use LLMs are having problems with hallucinations. (When I wrote about them less than a year ago there were 112 documented cases with lawyers who got called out in Damien Charlotin’s database; now there are 914. That’s 8x growth in less than 12 months!)

from_speaker: a lot of lawyers who use LLMs
with lawyers who got called out
our_interpretation: The knowledge qualifier does not turn the observation into a conditional forecast.
A lot means numerous documented lawyer incidents, not a majority or a measured proportion of all lawyers using LLMs.
The numerical assertion requires comparable database counts: 112 at an earlier point within the preceding year and 914 around February 12, 2026.
Eightfold means an approximately eightfold final-to-initial ratio, rather than an 800 percent increase.
Cases involving self-represented litigants cannot automatically be counted as cases involving lawyers.
The target period covers the preceding year through publication because the statement expressly compares an earlier count with now.
criteria.support_condition: Dated database records establish both counts within twelve months, show that the counted population matches the lawyer description, and document numerous lawyer hallucination incidents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable historical records establish materially different counts or timing, or establish that the totals described as lawyer cases include a materially different population.
